title: Locked Read-Modify-Write Ownership
description: Original multi-master AHB uses a requesting master's HLOCKx and the arbiter's bus-level HMASTLOCK indication to retain active ownership on the applicable arbitration/resource path through an indivisible sequence; future grant computation is not the same as ownership transfer.

phases.name: Request lock
phases.description: CPU asserts HLOCKx with HBUSREQx early enough for the arbiter to protect the upcoming sequence.

phases.name: Lock requested
phases.description: The request remains associated with the CPU's indivisible read-modify-write sequence.

phases.name: Locked active owner
phases.description: The arbiter identifies the active transfer sequence as locked and must not transfer active ownership on this arbitration path. It can still compute or signal a future grant if that indication cannot take effect early.

phases.name: Release boundary
phases.description: The final locked transfer completes; an IDLE after a locked sequence is recommended so arbitration can change cleanly.

phases.name: Read semaphore
phases.description: CPU reads the semaphore while retaining locked ownership on the shown path.

phases.name: Write semaphore
phases.description: CPU writes the updated semaphore before another master can use this protected arbitration/resource path. Independent aliases or paths need their own system-level protection.

phases.name: Request blocked
phases.description: DMA can request and the arbiter may compute its future grant, but the arbiter must not transfer ownership while HMASTLOCK identifies the locked sequence on this path. 'Blocked' here means blocked from becoming active owner, not prohibited from requesting or being selected for a future grant.

phases.name: DMA granted
phases.description: DMA can take ownership only after the locked sequence and its legal release boundary.
